$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Cosmos DB (SQL / Core API). See aws/s3.json for the contract.

azure.cosmos.account.crud.title: Database accounts (create, get, list, delete) over ARM

azure.cosmos.network_rules.title: Network rules (selected networks) and private endpoints
limitations: virtualNetworkRules (subnet must carry the Microsoft.AzureCosmosDB service endpoint, enabled for you), ipRules (valid IPv4 addresses/CIDRs), isVirtualNetworkFilterEnabled and publicNetworkAccess are real validated ARM state, and private endpoints (privatelink.documents.azure.com) with approve/reject are real control-plane resources. Data-plane requests are ENFORCED against ipRules / virtualNetworkRules (subnet needs the Microsoft.AzureCosmosDB service endpoint) / publicNetworkAccess=Disabled / private endpoints for a caller that declares its network identity with x-vyomi-source-ip / x-vyomi-source-subnet / x-vyomi-private-endpoint headers (403 Forbidden otherwise); a caller with no declared identity is only blocked by publicNetworkAccess=Disabled, since the simulator has no real source network. The account is named by x-vyomi-account / Host, or is the only Cosmos account.

azure.cosmos.data_explorer.title: Data Explorer: databases, containers and documents over the native Cosmos DB REST (SQL/Core API) data plane
limitations: The Cosmos data-plane store is a single keyspace shared by every Cosmos account in this Vyomi environment (no per-account partitioning) — a database id created under one account is visible from any other account's Data Explorer.

New Container validates the partition key definition (Hash = one path; hierarchical MultiHash version 2 = two or three distinct paths) and rejects a document whose partition key does not match the x-ms-documentdb-partitionkey header. Document ids are still unique per container, not per logical partition. A unique key policy and analytical store enablement are accepted the way the real form submits them but not enforced; only the indexing policy (on/off) round-trips for real.

azure.cosmos.query.title: SQL query (SELECT) over the Cosmos data plane
limitations: Covers a pragmatic SELECT subset: projection (incl. SELECT VALUE), TOP n, WHERE combining comparisons/IN/CONTAINS/STARTSWITH/ENDSWITH with a single logical operator throughout (AND-only or OR-only — mixed or parenthesized boolean expressions are not parsed), ORDER BY one field, OFFSET/LIMIT, and a top-level COUNT/VALUE COUNT aggregate; joins, subqueries, GROUP BY, other aggregate/system functions and stored procedures are not implemented.

azure.cosmos.default_consistency.title: Default consistency level
limitations: properties.consistencyPolicy is ENFORCED at the ARM contract level (defaultConsistencyLevel must be one of the 5 real values; BoundedStaleness requires maxStalenessPrefix in [10, 2147483647] and maxIntervalInSeconds in [5, 86400], same range Azure validates) — but every data-plane read in Vyomi is already strongly consistent, regardless of the configured level.

azure.cosmos.replicate_data_globally.title: Replicate data globally (region list, failover)
limitations: Add region and Manual Failover are ENFORCED for real: properties.locations is validated (unique region names, a 0-based gap-free failoverPriority sequence) and failoverPriorityChange really reassigns which region is failoverPriority 0. Vyomi still has one logical region underneath, so an added region never gets its own separately provisioned data-plane copy, and Service-Managed (automatic) Failover is an honest 'Not simulated' gap — Vyomi never triggers a failover on its own.

azure.cosmos.backup_restore.title: Backup & Restore policy
limitations: properties.backupPolicy is ENFORCED at the ARM contract level (backupPolicy.type, the Periodic interval/retention/redundancy ranges, the Continuous tier enum, and Azure's one-way Continuous-to-Periodic migration block all match the real API), but Vyomi never actually takes or restores a backup.

azure.cosmos.locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to the database account
limitations: Locks are only simulated at the resource scope (this account); subscription- and resource-group-scoped lock lists are an honest 'Not simulated' gap, same as the real Subscription/Resource group scope-switch buttons.

azure.cosmos.activity_log.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered ARM mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill). The timespan picker is ENFORCED (narrowing it to e.g. 'Last hour' really drops older events via eventTimestamp ge on the query), but severity/category filtering is not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

azure.cosmos.iam.title: Access control (IAM): role assignments and built-in role definitions over ARM
limitations: Role assignments and role definitions are real ARM resources (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions). The Role assignments list is now ENFORCED scoped to this account (plus its subscription/resource-group ancestors, matching real Azure's inherited-access view) instead of the whole subscription; Roles stays subscription-wide, which matches real Azure (built-in role definitions are listed tenant-wide too). 'Check access' / 'My access' evaluation is still not modelled — Vyomi never denies a console action based on a role assignment.

azure.cosmos.costmgmt.title: Cost Management for this account
limitations: Month-to-date real-Azure cost, list price per month and money saved are derived from the shared Cost Management engine over this account's ARM record (account-level list price; per-container RU/s and storage metering is not modelled).

azure.cosmos.addsearch.title: Add Azure AI Search (Cosmos DB)
limitations: A real search service, index, data source and indexer are created through Microsoft.Search, but Vyomi indexers only read Blob data: running the indexer on a cosmosdb data source ends in transientFailure with that message. Pulling Cosmos documents into an index is not implemented.

azure.cosmos.cors.title: CORS rules (properties.cors)
limitations: Rules are validated (at most 10; scheme://host origins, *.domain wildcards, methods, maxAgeInSeconds) and stored on the account. The Vyomi data plane does not add Access-Control headers from them.

azure.cosmos.dedicatedgateway.title: Dedicated gateway (databaseAccounts/services/SqlDedicatedGateway)
limitations: Provisioning is validated (NoSQL non-serverless accounts, size Cosmos.D4s/D8s/D16s, 1-5 instances) and the endpoint is derived. There is no integrated cache: requests through the gateway endpoint are not served.

azure.cosmos.dataencryption.title: Customer-managed key (keyVaultKeyUri)
limitations: The key URI shape, the existence of its Key Vault in this subscription and a managed identity are required; a customer-managed key cannot be removed. The key is looked up in the Key Vault keys data plane (400 KeyVaultKeyNotFound / KeyVaultKeyDisabled); that store is one keyspace shared by all vaults, so the lookup is by key name, not per vault, and data is not re-encrypted.

azure.cosmos.scale_ru.title: Scale: request-unit consumption from measured requests
limitations: RU charges are MODELLED from each measured request's size using Microsoft's published cost model (1 KB point read = 1 RU, 1 KB write ~ 5 RU) - not metered by a real RU engine. A manual or autoscale offer on a database (shared) or container (ARM sqlDatabases[/containers]/throughputSettings/default, validated: manual >= 400 step 100, autoscale max >= 1000 step 1000) IS enforced with 429 RequestRateTooLarge + x-ms-retry-after-ms over a trailing one-second window using that modelled charge (autoscale max is the limit; no step scaling, no per-partition 10k RU/s limit); each response carries x-ms-request-charge. Consumption is account-level (not split per container).
